p01-detector-title.text: Detector stage: apply an activation to each cell
p01-detector-title.name: p01-detector-title

p01-detector-p.text: Compare each cell with $0$. Clip negatives and keep positives, independently of position and neighbors.
p01-detector-p.name: p01-detector-p

p01-detector-why.text: Match: a strong positive response lights up.
p01-detector-why.name: p01-detector-why

p01-detector-why2.text: Mismatch: a negative response falls silent.
p01-detector-why2.name: p01-detector-why2

p01-detector-q.text: What does the detector do to $s$? Why call it a detector? Does it learn weights?
p01-detector-q.name: p01-detector-q

p01-detector-c.text: ReLU has no trainable weights. The preceding kernel learns.
p01-detector-c.name: p01-detector-c

p01-detector-nav.text: Week 6 · KP08 · 01/06 · Pause and predict before advancing
p01-detector-nav.name: p01-detector-nav

p02-four-te2.name: p02-four-te2

p02-four-q.text: Split the $4\times4$ map into four $2\times2$ blocks. What do max and average pooling return?
p02-four-q.name: p02-four-q

p02-four-c.text: The best summary depends on the task. Max pooling is common.
p02-four-c.name: p02-four-c

p02-four-nav.text: Week 6 · KP08 · 02/06 · Pause and predict before advancing
p02-four-nav.name: p02-four-nav

p04-channels-title.text: Pooling works per channel and has no weights
p04-channels-title.name: p04-channels-title

p04-channels-q.text: Max-pool $4\times4\times3$ with a $2\times2$ window and stride $2$. How many output channels and trainable weights?
p04-channels-q.name: p04-channels-q

p04-channels-c.text: Pool channels independently. There is no cross-channel sum.
p04-channels-c.name: p04-channels-c
